title: What official reviewers found
question: What have the State and the City's own departments reported about how San Francisco handles permits?
finding: 17 findings are drawn from 6 official documents. The State housing department's 2023 review (9 findings here) said San Francisco has the longest housing timelines in California, an average of 523 days to entitle a project and 605 more to issue a building permit on 2022 data, and ordered the City to remove discretion from code-compliant housing approvals and to standardize permitting after entitlement. The City's own annual reports record review targets of 21, 30 and 14 days at Planning and 63% of counter permits handled within two business days at Building Inspection.
how: Each row is one finding from an official review or performance report saved in the collection, put in plain words, with a short quotation that the script checks against the saved text of the document, and the figures in the summary checked the same way.
limits: These are the reviewers' findings, not this project's. The State review rests on research interviews and on data the City reported; departments' annual reports describe their own performance. The Mayor's 2025 permit reform directive and the 2018 directive on accessory dwelling units are saved only as scanned images without text and are not quoted. Reviews already in the project library (the Budget and Legislative Analyst, the Controller's public integrity reviews, the Civil Grand Jury) are reported in the permit records section, not repeated here.
